note: Intake prompts for /start, one at a time, in the user's words. A number they aren't sure of is kept as they said it. 'Don't know' is a valid answer.
common: For each role: the product or system you worked on, who used it, and how big it was (users, requests per second, data volume, money moved).
Your stack in each role: languages, frameworks, databases, cloud, and how deep (built from scratch, owned, maintained, used).
A design decision you drove: the options, what you chose, why, and what happened afterwards.
A production incident you handled: what broke, how you found it, how long it took, and what changed after.
Something you made faster, cheaper or more reliable, with the before and after numbers if you have them (latency, cost, error rate, build time).
Team: who you worked with, whether you led, mentored or interviewed anyone, and how many.
Open source, side projects, talks, patents, writing, awards, certifications: with links and years.

backend: The services or APIs you owned: what they did, their traffic, latency targets and dependencies.
Data stores you designed or migrated: schema, size, indexing, consistency choices.
Queues, caches or async work you built, and why.
full-stack: A feature you built end to end: UI, API and data, and how you shipped it.
How you measured whether it worked (adoption, conversion, errors).
frontend: Apps or components you owned, the framework, and the size of the codebase or team.
Performance or accessibility work, with numbers (load time, Core Web Vitals, bundle size).
mobile: Apps you shipped: platform, users or downloads, ratings, crash-free rate.
Release process, offline support, or performance work you did.
platform-sre: Infrastructure you ran: cloud, cluster size, number of services, deploy frequency.
SLOs you owned and your on-call record; incidents you led.
Cost or reliability improvements, with numbers.
data-eng: Pipelines you built: sources, volume per day, latency, tools.
Data quality or cost work, with numbers.
ml-eng: Models or LLM features you shipped: the task, the data, the metric, and the result in production.
How you served, monitored and evaluated them.
security: Security programmes or tools you owned; vulnerabilities found or fixed; audits passed.
eng-management: Team size and shape, hiring you did, attrition, and how you ran delivery.
A hard people situation and how you handled it.
What your team shipped and its impact.
qa-sdet: Test frameworks you built or owned; coverage, flakiness and run time before and after.
Bugs or incidents your tests caught.
